name: coding-life
title: A small public set of coding sessions

conditions.data: coding-agent-life-v1 from the agentmemory project: 15 invented sessions on a Rust command-line tool, 15 questions with the sessions that answer them; public, checksums pinned in the script
conditions.pipeline: the sessions archived into a fresh ctx database, then ctx search with each question as typed
conditions.scoring: the first five distinct sessions among the ranked turns; no model involved

summary: The only public set of coding-session questions found. It is tiny and invented, and plain grep nearly ties on it, so it is a check that nothing is broken and not a measure of how good a tool is.

metrics.label: Questions with every evidence session in the first 5
Questions with at least one evidence session in the first 5

baseline: the scores its authors publish on the same files: their keyword component found every evidence session for 14 of 15 questions, and their grep baseline for 15 of 15 (measured 2026-10-28)
meaning: ctx clears the check. It says little more than that: the set is 15 invented sessions, and grep does as well. A harder public set of coding sessions does not exist yet.
bar: every evidence session found for at least 14 of 15 questions
